tasks.gr8-classification-of-matter-and-periodi: Topic: Classification of matter and periodic table. Cover elements, compounds, mixtures, metals, non-metals, solutions, and periodic-table basics. Ask Grade 8 learners to classify substances accurately, distinguish mixtures from compounds, and interpret simple periodic-table information.
tasks.gr8-chemical-reactions-acids-and-bases-t: Topic: Chemical reactions, acids and bases. Cover physical versus chemical change, evidence of reaction, indicators, acids, bases, neutralisation, and suitable separation methods for mixtures. Ask Grade 8 learners to identify reaction evidence, read indicator results, and choose appropriate practical methods.
tasks.gr8-static-electricity-t3: Topic: Static electricity. Cover charging by friction as a transfer of electrons only (protons and neutrons do not move), the material that loses electrons becoming positive and the one that gains them becoming negative, like charges repelling and unlike charges attracting, a charged ruler attracting small pieces of paper, and the discharge of electrons causing a spark or shock especially in dry air. Learners do not need to memorise which charge a material gets. Ask Grade 8 learners to predict forces and explain charging.
tasks.gr8-electric-circuits-current-t3: Topic: Circuits and current electricity (qualitative; no V = IR, no calculations). Cover a circuit as a complete conducting pathway from a cell through wires and a device and back, the need for a closed circuit, the components (cell or battery as a chemical source of energy, conducting wires, switch, bulb filament and resistors that oppose the flow of current), electric current as a flow of charges, and the heating effect (filament, fuse, short circuit), the magnetic effect (electromagnet) and the chemical effect (electrolysis of water into hydrogen and oxygen, of copper chloride into copper and chlorine). Ask Grade 8 learners to interpret circuit diagrams and explain effects.
tasks.gr8-series-parallel-circuits-t3: Topic: Series and parallel circuits, treated QUALITATIVELY as the Grade 8 CAPS says (the effects of resistance are treated qualitatively by observing the brightness of a bulb). Series: one pathway, the same current everywhere, and every resistor added in series decreases the overall current so the bulbs get dimmer. Parallel: two or more pathways, and the overall current increases when more resistors are added in parallel. Other output devices (beepers, buzzers, LEDs, motors). Different conductors such as copper and nichrome have different resistance. Do NOT use V = IR or equivalent resistance formulae. Ask Grade 8 learners to predict and compare brightness and pathways.
tasks.gr8-visible-light-t3: Topic: Visible light. Cover light from luminous objects travelling in straight lines by radiation at 300 000 km per second in empty space, the spectrum (violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, red) with violet the highest frequency and red the lowest, dispersion by a prism and in a rainbow, opaque and transparent substances and shadows, colour by absorption and reflection (red, black and white objects), reflection with the angle of incidence equal to the angle of reflection measured from the normal (smooth and rough surfaces), seeing light, and refraction towards the normal on entering a transparent medium and away on leaving. Ask Grade 8 learners to explain and to give the angle of reflection.
